citations.title: Announcement - HSBC Holdings plc Annual Results 2025

sentences.text: HSBC said in September 2026 that Group CFO Pam Kaur will retire, with the board searching internally and externally for a successor and Kaur staying until the 2027 AGM or earlier.

Board changes effective 5 August 2026 saw Richard Meddings take over as Group Audit Committee chair from Brendan Nelson, who became Group Chairman, while Alison Platt joined as an independent non-executive director on 1 October 2026 and will chair the Group Remuneration Committee from February 2027.
Insurance CEO Edward Moncreiffe resigned in August 2026, and David Rice was named first Chief AI Officer in March 2026.

citations.title: Banker of the year 2026: HSBC's Georges Elhedery - Euromoney

sentences.text: Georges Elhedery, CEO since September 2024, quickly collapsed HSBC's matrix structure into four units and scaled back Western investment banking, targeting roughly $1.5bn of annualised cost reductions by end-2026, later raised to $2bn, with 15 non-strategic businesses exited since 2025.

For 2025 the total ordinary dividend was $0.75 per share, or $12.9bn, up 14%, and $6bn of buybacks took total returns to $18.9bn, with a share price up more than 49% and total shareholder return above 57%.
Buybacks were temporarily suspended in connection with the proposed privatisation of Hang Seng Bank.

sentences.quote: The simplification programme has consequently allowed the bank to reduce managing director positions by 15% under Elhedery, cutting global staffing costs by 8%. The restructuring also led to a reduced executive committee from 18 to 12 members
sentences.text: On governance, managing director positions fell 15%, the executive committee shrank from 18 to 12, and 60% of revenue now sits under a single accountable executive.

sentences.text: HSBC Holdings delivered record 2025 profit before tax of $36.6bn excluding notable items, with revenue up 5% to $71.0bn and return on average tangible equity of 17.2% excluding notable items.

We completed two share buybacks in respect of 2025 worth a total of $6bn
sentences.text: Capital returns are substantial: a total 2025 dividend of $0.75 per share plus two buy-backs worth $6bn, supported by a CET1 ratio of 14.9%.
Simplification is running ahead of plan, with HSBC now intending to action about $2.0bn of annualised simplification savings by FY26 against restructuring costs of roughly $1.8bn.
Portfolio reshaping toward Asia continues through exits including Singapore insurance, Australia retail and Egypt retail, plus a strategic review of Turkiye retail and domestic SMEs.
Growth is skewed to fee businesses, including 16% growth in securities services on new Asian client mandates.
